subject: CedarBridge mortgage pilot: success metrics, ops owners and decision gates
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Evan Greene <evan@cedarbridge.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cedarbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: CedarBridge mortgage pilot: success metrics, ops owners and decision gates

Hi Evan / Marta —

Thanks again for the great discussion today. Quick post-call recap and a proposed structure for the pilot so we can align expectations and get started next week: 

Summary goals (customer-facing):
- Validate Redwood inference end-to-end on your mortgage-document Q&A workflow.
- Demonstrate sustained latency and cost under a representative throughput.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p95 generation latency under 200ms for single-turn Q&A on a 512-token budget (measured from request receive to first-token).
- Throughput: baseline of 250 requests/sec with linear scaling to 500 req/s for burst windows; sustained 250 req/s during the pilot window.
- Cost target: average model cost <= $0.003 / token for the evaluation workload (including both prompt + generated tokens).
- Quality: 88% accuracy on labelled NPS-style answers (we'll run a blind eval set of 1,200 Q&A pairs) + <6% hallucination rate on a curated holdout set.
- Operational: no more than 1 incident causing degraded availability >10 minutes in the pilot window.

Evaluation plan & timings:
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange sample snippets and the evaluation spreadsheet (you to provide).
2) Week 1: Redwood runs smoke tests on a 100-query validation set and shares performance & cost profile.
3) Week 2: Full 1,200-query quality run + throughput ramp to 250 req/s; share readout and proposed remediation if gates fail.
4) Week 3: Optional tuning (batching, quantization profile) and final readout for go/no-go.

Ops & owners (Redwood / CedarBridge):
- Redwood technical lead / contact: Monica Patel (pilot orchestration + instrumentation).
- Redwood infra / network: Karthik Iyer (VPC & egress configuration).
- Redwood AE / commercial: me (Priyom) — timelines, deal coordination, procurement intake.
- CedarBridge product: Evan Greene (evaluation owner).
- CedarBridge security: Marta Lopez (compliance sign-off).

Immediate asks for CedarBridge:
- Share a zipped sample of 1,200 de-identified Q&A pairs + an initial 100-query smoke subset by Thu 31 Jul. (attachment: sample format in cedarbridge_sample_snippets.jsonl)
- Confirm whether the procurement team needs a bespoke SLA template (I attached our pilot SLA template for reference).
- Availability for a 30-min technical kickoff with Karthik & Monica on Fri (31 Jul) between 10–12 PT.

I'll update the HubSpot record and send a calendar invite once we have the smoke dataset.

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

—
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_pilot_sla_template.pdf (1 page)
From: Evan Greene <evan@cedarbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cedarbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CedarBridge mortgage pilot: success metrics, ops owners and decision gates

Thanks Priyom — very clear and helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Throughput: we want to start with a conservative baseline of 150–200 req/s for Week 2 (our UAT env has limits). If the smoke tests look good we can ramp to 250 fast, but can you confirm Redwood's ability to throttle/rate limit without impacting latency?

2) Cost target: $0.003/token looks reasonable as a long-term target, but for the pilot we only need a relative cost profile (i.e., compare candidate models + quantization). Can you include per-model cost breakdowns in the Week 1 smoke readout?

We will deliver the 1,200 de-identified pairs (and the 100 smoke subset) by Thu 31 Jul — I'm looping procurement into this thread (procurement@cedarbridge.com) to start the paperwork.

Also, Friday 31 Jul 10:15 PT works for the kickoff.

Best,
Evan

Karthik — forwarding the CedarBridge notes and their kickoff at 10:15 PT on Fri. Key infra items for our checklist: 
- Confirm VPC peering and egress IP allowlist (they may want to lock down endpoints).
- Prepare a small reserved pool to ensure steady performance at 150–250 req/s during Week 2.
- Instrumentation: we'll need an agreed set of metrics (p95 latency, 99th, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec) pushed to the shared Drive readout for the pilot.

Also: include a short note about tokenization differences across models in the Week 1 readout (Evan asked for per-model cost breakdowns).

—Monica

Thanks Evan — perfect. Quick confirmations: 
- We'll run Week 2 at a conservative baseline of 150 req/s and have an automated ramp to 250 req/s if the smoke tests meet latency & error-rate gates.
- Week 1 smoke readout will include per-model cost/token, tokenization delta, and a small table mapping latency-to-batching-config used.
- We'll publish all instrumentation dashboards to the shared Drive link I added above and attach the pilot SLA template for procurement review.

Next steps (actionable):
- Evan / Marta: upload de-identified 1,200 Q&A examples + 100-smoke subset to the Drive folder by Thu 31 Jul EOD.
- Procurement: if you want a redline to the attached pilot SLA (redwood_pilot_sla_template.pdf), please let us know and we'll loop Legal.
- Monica / Karthik: I'll send the calendar invite for Fri 31 Jul 10:15 PT and include a short agenda (kickoff + infra validation + evaluation plan).

If anyone prefers a different success-weighting (we proposed equal weighting across latency/throughput/cost/quality), say so in this thread before the kickoff.

—
Priyom Das
